reuse.why: All six link handlers now route through one linkBankSyncAccount, but the helper hand-rolls the sync-source union instead of using AccountSyncSource/SYNC_PROVIDERS (to which fintegra is never added), re-writes unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount clearing block, and the Fintegra download copies the Akahu one.

duplication.why: The refactor removes five copies of the link flow, but the take-over step inlines the same eight-column clearing that unlinkAccount does and downloadFintegraTransactions is a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions.

placement.why: The duplicate-link, closed-account and take-over rules sit in the shared link helper in accounts/app.ts, the download in sync.ts and the URL in server-config, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the four steps' needs plus release notes and a focused test; no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: One link definition with explicit per-provider variation (bankKey, newAccountFields, cloudFileId, syncedTables) is easy to own; the duplicated unlink clearing and the off-registry syncSource union are the weak spots.

bypasses_abstraction.where: linkBankSyncAccount clears the old holder with its own db.updateAccount block instead of reusing unlinkAccount's clearing logic, and declares its own syncSource literal union instead of AccountSyncSource/SYNC_PROVIDERS.

disguised_duplication.where: The unlink clearing in linkBankSyncAccount and downloadFintegraTransactions in sync.ts are plain copies, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount gained only replaceExistingLink (step 4); the duplicate-link and closed-account checks are general rules applied to every provider, and all six handlers including Fintegra call the helper.
